title: FIPS gate on RESET — correct, touches crypto state
description: Why it is right: ioctl_reset() calls ops->fips_gate() before ops->sess_reset(). sess_reset() touches algorithm-internal state: it clears digest state machines, zeroes IV slots, and resets key schedule tracking within the provider's ctx. Under FIPS 140-3, any operation that reads or modifies state within the FIPS cryptographic boundary must be gated. A reviewer might argue: 'RESET is administrative housekeeping, not a crypto operation — skip the gate for performance.' But sess_reset() operates on the same provider-managed ctx that holds the keying material and streaming state. Touching that ctx without gating is indistinguishable from a crypto operation from the FIPS boundary's perspective. The gate is cheap (an atomic read in the common case) and mandatory.
close_reason: confirmed correct: FIPS gate on RESET is required — sess_reset touches provider ctx which contains keying material; skipping the gate on 'administrative' ops would be a FIPS 140-3 audit finding
